exposure: Obstetric Cholestasis (diagnosed by serum bile acid values > 8 mmol/L)
outcome: maternal outcomes (indication for induction, mode of delivery)
neonatal outcomes (reduced APGAR, meconium passage, NICU admission, stillbirths, neonatal mortality)
cohort: 42 pregnant women from 1302 births in SUH in 2018 who had serum bile acid values > 8 mmol/L.
finding: The suspected incidence of Obstetric Cholestasis was 3.2% (n=42), which is significantly higher than the stated 0.7% across multi-ethnic populations, and no neonatal mortality was observed.
mod_finding: Among women with Obstetric Cholestasis, 43% (n=20) had a Cesarean section and 57% (n=25) had a vaginal birth.
